newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer at fresh one-year highs.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer at fresh one-year highs.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer at fresh, one-year highs on Wednesday in good volume as sharp gains from the previous session's close were followed through.
The spot month closed at its highest since mid-May 1996 on the weekly charts. July set a fresh life-of-contract high for the second consecutive session.
But no fresh news lay behind Wednesday gains, just on-going concern about tight physical supplies and potential and actual labor problems at production plants, dealers said.
"The technicals on the charts look very good," a broker said. "There is a very steady underlying market."
July COMEX settled 1.70 cents firmer at 121.80 cents per lb, traded 121.90 to 120.60 cents. Spot June went out 1.85 cents firmer at 121.55 cents.
The LME cash to three months backwardation so far this week has surged some $40 to $101/$105, but COMEX June to July remained in contango.

LME stocks have resumed their downward trend this week, dipping a combined 5,100 tonnes Monday through Wednesday, though the latter day's dip was a more modest 600 tonnes. The London exchange stocks now total 127,525 tonnes.
